consensus_summary: Modern Christian teaching primarily treats Issachar as symbolizing discernment or ‘understanding of the times’ (1 Chr 12:32), with common historic alternatives of burden-bearing servitude (Gen 49 donkey), wages/reward (name etymology), and secondary motifs of tents/prosperity or scholarship; no single settled consensus across eras.
book_summary: Issachar is the hireling who owns the field: strong donkey to carry, humble to bow, settled in tents, discerning appointed times, rich enough to feed a king, willing to enter the valley to save Israel; also Virgo in the east with sapphire and the full moon.
consensus_core_identification: Discernment of the times / strategic insight (primary modern) or strong burden-bearing donkey/servant (primary historic)
book_core_identification: Composite hireling-owner of the field uniting donkey strength/humility, tents, time-discernment, royal provision, and valley courage (plus celestial Virgo/sapphire/moon)
boundary_disagreement: Book elevates and unifies secondary or alternative traits (hire/ownership of field, feeding a king, valley march, tents) into the single core portrait and adds celestial assignments absent from consensus; consensus keeps discernment or donkey as separable primaries and treats other motifs as lesser alternatives.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap on the shared scriptural traits (donkey, tents, times, hire). The book does not replace or deny the consensus referents; it preserves them while broadening the identification into one synthetic figure and extending it with astronomical correspondences. Extra celestial detail and tighter unification refine rather than diverge from the recognizable tribal-symbol category.
strongest_objection: The Virgo/sapphire/full-moon layer and the precise ‘hireling who owns the field’ unification have no foothold in the consensus readings or the listed alternatives, so the book’s full core may be judged partly extrinsic.
